# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## The grading contract: `hard_no_recalc` makes a formula unscoreable (measured on the 40 baseline traces)

This run uses `SPREADSHEETBENCH_SCORING=hard` with `SPREADSHEETBENCH_REWARD_RECALC=0`. The grader
reads **stored cell values** and never recalculates. openpyxl writes a formula as `<f>` with **no
`<v>`**, so a formula cell reads back as **empty** and can never match — however correct it is.

- **Confirmed by direct measurement of the baseline (pre-RESULT, from the traces themselves, not a
  guess):** tasks whose solution code writes formulas pass **0 of 13**; tasks that write literals
  pass **18 of 27**. Seven failing tasks (37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942) carry
  `test_case_results=[1]` alongside `test_case_results_no_recalc=[0]` — they solved the spreadsheet
  problem and lost only on the stored-value contract.
- **Refuted:** "the instruction wording tells you when a formula is wanted." 3 of 4 sampled
  *passing* tasks also ask for "a formula". Wording is not a discriminator, so the compute-in-Python
  rule must be unconditional.
- **Refuted:** "the `#N/A` cluster is input NaN propagated through." 54144 and 37456 never read a
  value from the input (no `data_only=True` in either trace); the error tokens come from evaluating
  the agent's own defective formula (Excel-365-only `TEXTSPLIT`; a `$A$2` anchor where the header is
  on row 3). The fix is "your logic is wrong", not "don't propagate".
- Awaiting a RESULT for cand_0001 to confirm the prose fix converts these.

## Verification is the second-largest lever, and it was structurally discouraged

- **Measured:** **39 of 40** baseline traces never re-opened the file they wrote. The single trace
  that did (416-15) passed. The agent read `[Code executed successfully with no output]` as success.
- **Mechanism found:** when `task_template.md` is absent the adapter uses its built-in
  `_TASK_TEMPLATE`, which contains *"once that file exists, you are done"*. Creating
  `task_template.md` at all is what suppresses that line. A future iteration that deletes the file
  brings the line back.
- **Corollary, measured:** the freed budget is already there. 46897 resubmitted a byte-identical
  block 28×, 6698 29×, 55049 27× — the wasted rounds exceed an audit's cost tenfold. The missing
  pieces were a stop condition and a defined next action, not turns.
- **Verified constraint on any audit snippet:** 5 of the 18 passing tasks have legitimately blank
  gold cells (382-10 79% — its task *is* to delete values; 395-36 67%; 402-43 65%; 142-12 40%;
  560-12 33% padding). Treating blank as a defect false-alarms on exactly those 5. Blank must be a
  judgement ("is a value expected here?"), never a reflex, and the prose must forbid padding a range
  to look full.
- Also verified: an unbounded audit print floods context (1280 lines on 9569, ~4451 cells on 48921).
  Cap the sample and print an aggregate count.

## Two mechanical facts about this adapter worth not rediscovering

- `spreadsheet_content` is `pandas.read_excel(..., header=0)`: the preview's **column labels are
  Excel row 1**, and preview row `i` is **Excel row `i + 2`**. 59196 read `ws["D1"]` (blank, its
  header is row 2) and wrote `None` everywhere; 227-40's `iloc[13]` landed on Excel row 15,
  producing exactly its observed 12/20.
- `extract_code` takes only the **FIRST** ```python block in a reply; the rest are silently
  discarded. 46897's opening reply had 6 blocks, so its diagnostic `print`s never ran and it
  resolved a genuine ambiguity by speculation.
- `openpyxl.utils.range_boundaries` **rejects a sheet-qualified range** — split on `!` and strip
  quotes before calling it. `openpyxl`'s `ArrayFormula` is neither `str` nor numeric, so a
  `startswith("=")` check misses it while an `isinstance` type check catches it.
- An **empty** `prompt.md` means "no system message"; a **missing** one falls back to
  `_DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`. The two are not equivalent.
- 402-43 passes while its pandas round trip **silently drops Sheet1** — grading was confined to
  Sheet2. A latent fragility, not a real pass of the whole workbook.

## Not touching a cell does NOT preserve it — openpyxl erases input formulas on save

The most counter-intuitive fact in this benchmark, and it punishes *correct* restraint. When a
cell in `answer_position` holds a formula in the **input**, `load_workbook(p)` → `wb.save(out)`
rewrites it as `<f>` with **no `<v>`**. Excel displayed a number there; your saved file does not.
So "I wasn't asked to change G1, so I left it alone" **destroys** G1 and the grader reads it empty.

- **Measured (init-vs-golden sweep over all 40 val tasks):** 7 tasks have an input formula inside
  `answer_position` — 267-18, 382-10, 48620, 53647, 56563, 6698, 7902. The 6 passing ones survive
  only because the instruction makes them overwrite every such cell anyway; **267-18 is the one
  where a formula cell must be preserved, and it is the one that fails.**
- **Verified by execution:** reading the input twice (`data_only=False` to detect a formula,
  `data_only=True` to recover the cached value) and writing the cached value back makes 267-18
  reproduce golden exactly, and reproduces all 28 cells of 7902 (already passing).
- **Corollary:** 7902's trace discovered this by accident — its audit showed 16 FORMULA cells it
  had not written, and it recovered them with `data_only=True`. That accident is why it passes.
- **Caveat that must ship with the rule:** use the cached value only to *preserve* a cell. For a
  cell the instruction asks you to change, the cache may be stale or hold the very `#NUM!`/
  `#VALUE!` the user wants fixed (56563, 6698, 55049 are exactly this) — compute those.

## The workbook usually contains the answer's specification; the prose is the unreliable part

These are help-forum posts, so the sheet nearly always carries a worked example — pre-filled cells
in `answer_position`, or a labelled block (`The Result I'm after`, `Result what i am expecting`).
Two distinct ways ignoring it loses a task, both measured:

- **Geometry.** 227-40's demo block is *header + 3 data rows*, so the output block is too. The
  agent mapped input data row 1 → range row 1, dropping the header and shifting everything by one
  → exactly the observed 12-of-20 coverage. **Verified:** taking the geometry from the demo block
  reproduces golden A14:E17 on all 4 rows.
- **Rule derivation.** 48527's two pre-filled cells contradict the literal reading of the
  instruction. Its trace says *"But the preview shows D2='Apple'"* and then **overrides the
  evidence with the prose**, writing `None` over a cell whose expected value is its own original
  input. A pre-filled cell is proof that the rule covers its row; if your reading blanks it, the
  reading is wrong, not the example.
- **Blast-radius fact for anyone tightening this:** 20 passing tasks have pre-filled cells in
  range. 13 keep them unchanged in gold; 7 (142-12, 59595, 9569, 9726, 6698, 56563, 48620) change
  them — and in all 7 the instruction explicitly asks for that change. So "reproduce the example"
  must never become "never overwrite a filled cell".

## Counting tasks are lost on one endpoint, not on the logic

43436 had the right layout, grouping, types and record set, and still scored 0: it coded *"not
closed before the first day of M"* as `closed >= first_day_of_M`, which counts everything that
closed *inside* M as still open at the end of M. **Verified:** `closed is None or closed >
end_of_M` reproduces all 15 golden cells across all 5 departments. The scorer's signature for this
class is diagnostic — full coverage, right types, *"N cell(s) hold a number HIGHER than expected"*.
Double-negated windows ("not closed before X and not created after Y") should be restated
positively before coding. An empty "closed"/"returned" date means **still open**, not missing data.

## An audit snippet must be executed against the real workbooks before shipping — twice now it hid a bug

cand_0001's audit (accepted, +0.450) shipped with a latent defect: `isinstance(v, (int,float,bool,
str))` classifies every **`datetime`** as `FORMULA-OBJECT`. Running the snippet verbatim over all
40 tasks against a simulated correct solution raised false alarms on **416-15, 80-42, 9726 — all
passing, all date-valued** — and crashed with `KeyError` on 395-36 and 402-43, whose answer sheet
does not exist in the input. Neither is visible by reading the prose. The widened check is
`SCALAR = (int, float, bool, str, datetime.datetime, datetime.date, datetime.time,
datetime.timedelta)`. **Method worth keeping: build the "perfect answer" file (golden values as
literals on top of the real input), run the snippet on all 40, and require zero false alarms on
the passing set before shipping.** Also note the one *legitimate* `ERASED` report is 382-10, whose
task is to delete values — any input-vs-output comparison needs that carve-out stated in prose.
